channel.title: LIZI STACK — Notes
channel.description: Notes on recommender systems, LLMs, agent engineering, experiments, and long-term thinking.

item.title: Evaluating RAG Beyond Plausible Answers
item.description: Decompose RAG failures across retrieval, context construction, and generation so each result points to an actionable change.

item.title: Agents Need Explainable Traces, Not Just More Logs
item.description: Once an agent calls tools, changes state, and replans, conventional request logs are no longer enough to explain success or failure.

item.title: Why Better Offline Ranking Does Not Guarantee Better Online Results
item.description: Offline metrics are evidence, not a conclusion; data splits, exposure bias, and user segments determine whether that evidence is trustworthy.

item.title: Why This Blog Exists: A Version History for Technical Growth
item.description: I want a record of learning, engineering judgement, and long-term thinking that can be revisited and tested.

item.title: Reading Transformer: Why Attention Could Replace Recurrence
item.description: A close reading of scaled dot-product attention, multi-head attention, positional encoding, and the engineering conditions that made Transformer consequential.

item.title: Write the Learning Process, Not Only the Model Conclusion
item.description: A useful learning note is not a tutorial paraphrase. It keeps the question, the experiment path, and the boundary of the conclusion together.

item.title: Keep a Ledger for Every Experiment
item.description: An experiment note is not a diary; it is a small contract covering the hypothesis, cost, evidence, and next decision.

item.title: Reading DeepFM: Learning Low- and High-Order Feature Interactions Together
item.description: How shared embeddings connect the FM and deep branches, and why the architecture remains a useful recommender-systems baseline.

item.title: How Deep Should I Learn a New Technology?
item.description: Depth should follow frequency, the cost of being wrong, and whether the technology forms part of your core judgment.

item.title: What a Recommender-Model Experiment Should Leave Behind
item.description: More useful than remembering that a metric improved is keeping how the problem was defined, how the experiment was designed, and where the conclusion stops.

item.title: Reading ESMM: Modeling Post-Click Conversion in the Entire Space
item.description: How the exposure-click-conversion probability chain helps ESMM address sample-selection bias and sparse supervision in CVR estimation.

item.title: Reading ReAct: Closing the Loop Between Reasoning and Action
item.description: How interleaved Thought, Action, and Observation trajectories connect language reasoning to tools—and what production agents still need beyond the prompt.

item.title: Leave a Table for an Unfinished Agent Idea
item.description: An engineering experiment is not a product plan. It records hypotheses, prototypes, and explorations that do not yet have an answer.
